subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to dropped-media diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the shared `tools.fs.roots` design owns host-local root expansion, or should Telegram define its own outbound media root contract here?
rationale: The current failure crosses a user-visible message delivery problem and a host-file read/upload security boundary, so automation should not choose whether to broaden accepted local paths or keep this issue diagnostics-only.

options.title: Diagnostics Here, Root Policy Elsewhere
options.body: Keep this issue focused on reasoned Telegram/media drop diagnostics and let the shared root-policy item or approved filesystem-roots design define path expansion.

options.title: Telegram-Specific Root Contract
options.body: Use this issue to add a Telegram outbound media root config surface with schema, docs, security review, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document Managed Roots Only
options.body: Decline new root expansion for now and only document the supported managed roots and message-tool workaround.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics Here, Root Policy Elsewhere
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on reasoned Telegram/media drop diagnostics and let the shared root-policy item or approved filesystem-roots design define path expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the shared outbound media access policy that this decision would change.
